text:
Maya Chen: Quick weekly pulse for AcmeConv — token usage is up 24% WoW, but down 5% QoQ. Throughput steady during weekday mornings, a couple mid-day spikes. p95 latency moved from ~260ms -> ~310ms (yesterday peak). Error rate jumped from 0.9% to 2.4% in the 12:00-14:00 UTC window. Spend is +17% WoW (mainly due to higher non-cached prefixes + larger model fallbacks).

Jin Park: Sharing the metric slices I pulled:
```sql
-- tokens and errors by hour (last 7d)
SELECT hour, SUM(tokens) as tokens, SAFE_DIVIDE(SUM(errors), SUM(requests)) as error_rate
FROM `redwood-prod.metrics.acquire`
WHERE customer = 'acmeconv' AND ts >= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)
GROUP BY hour
ORDER BY hour;
```
Results: tokens concentrated 11:00-13:00 UTC, error_rate spike coincides with a small set of long-concat prompts.

Omar Patel: tl;dr probable cause = cache miss + fallback to a medium-precision variant that unexpectedly increased tail latency and triggered transient 502s. Logs show a brief surge of model-fallback events at 12:05 UTC (approx 12m).

Priya Singh: AcmeConv started a targeted onboarding email workflow on Mon -> could explain the burst. They also enabled a dataset upload feature yesterday which might create longer prompts. I flagged product contact to check.

Maya Chen: Impact summary for CS/AE:
- Customer experience: Some timeouts for synth-sessions, reported by 2 end-users (support tickets).
- Business: +17% spend this week vs baseline (they're on committed plan, but this accelerates burn).
- Renewal risk: low-to-medium if costs keep rising and latencies persist.

Jin Park: Raw quick numbers:
- 7d tokens: +24% WoW, QoQ -5%
- p50: 85ms -> 92ms (small)
- p95: 260ms -> 310ms
- error rate (12:00-14:00): 0.9% -> 2.4%
- avg request size (tokens): 430 -> 560 (so more long-context usage)

Omar Patel: Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Short-term: Enable request-level throttling for heavy prefix paths and route to cached model variant.
2) Mid-term: Add a fallback policy to prefer quantized variant during bursts (we can test on a canary).
3) Ops: Increase KV cache TTL for their session patterns by 30% to reduce cold-miss churn.

Priya Singh: I'll coordinate a 30-min enablement call with AcmeConv to walk them through batching best-practices and prefix trimming. Suggested times: Thu 15:00 or Fri 10:00 UTC.

Maya Chen: Action items (owners):
- Jin: add a dedicated dashboard slice for AcmeConv long-context requests + annotate the 12:05 spike (due EOD).
- Omar: roll canary policy for quantized fallback tomorrow 09:00 UTC and monitor for p95 regressions.
- Priya: schedule enablement call and confirm whether their dataset upload caused longer prompts.
- Maya: draft a one-off spend report + credit recommendation if we see repeat spikes.

deploy-bot: deploy 2065.31 started by omar at 09:00 UTC — applying canary fallback policy to 5% of traffic. :rocket:

Jin Park: Added dashboard link: https://console.redwood.ai/d/metrics/acmeconv?from=now-7d&to=now (pinning to the channel)

Maya Chen: Thanks — please update this thread once the canary has 30m of stable metrics. Will follow up on credits if spend continues. :thumbsup:
